extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of philosophy and aesthetics (readers of Kant's Critique of Judgment)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and conceptual distinctions for judging the sublime in aesthetics: definitions, the role of imagination vs. reason, mathematical vs. dynamic sublime, conditions for a "pure" aesthetic judgement, and the modal/cultural prerequisites for such judgements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of the Sublime
rubrics_metrics.description: “the sublime is that in comparison with which everything else is small.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text emphasises this concise formula and immediately draws out that the sublime is not a property of any sensible object but of our Ideas and of a state of mind produced by certain representations. The mere ability to think what is absolutely great (the infinite) reveals a faculty of mind surpassing sensibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sublime resides in the subject's state of mind, not in natural objects
rubrics_metrics.description: True sublimity must be sought only in the mind of the judging subject, not in the natural object which occasions the feeling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objects (e.g., shapeless mountain masses, raging sea) are not inherently sublime; the judgement of sublimity arises when the subject's Imagination is inadequate to its Ideas and feels elevated. Emphasise subjective origin when evaluating claims of sublimity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction: mathematical vs. aesthetical estimation of magnitude
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematical estimation of magnitude proceeds by concepts of number (no maximum); aesthetical (intuition/eye) estimation is subjective and admits a maximum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sublimity is linked to the aesthetical estimation reaching a subjectively maximal measure—an absolute magnitude for the judging subject that mathematical number alone cannot produce. When judging magnitude, note whether the reaction stems from numerical comparison or from an intuition hitting its aesthetic maximum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two operations of the Imagination: apprehension and comprehension
rubrics_metrics.description: Apprehension (apprehensio) can proceed ad infinitum; comprehension (comprehensio aesthetica) has a limit—the maximum of aesthetic comprehension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sublime arises when apprehension outstrips comprehension so that earlier parts of a series vanish while the Imagination strives to take in the whole. Examples and anti-patterns: standing too close or too far from the Pyramids reduces the effect; similar bewilderment occurs entering St. Peter's.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement of 'pure' aesthetical judgement for the sublime (disinterested and non-teleological)
rubrics_metrics.description: A pure aesthetic judgement on the sublime must be disinterested and not mixed with teleological judgements (no appeal to the object's purpose).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not ground the judgement of the sublime in objects whose form or size is determined by human purpose (buildings, pillars) or in natural objects whose concepts have definite purposes (animals). The appropriate locus is 'rude nature' that contains magnitude without purposeful form or actual danger.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monstrous vs. Colossal distinction (anti-patterns)
rubrics_metrics.description: An object is monstrous if by its size it destroys the purpose constituting its concept; the 'colossal' is almost too great for any presentation, bordering on monstrous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing supposed sublimity, check whether the object's size undermines its concept (monstrous) or merely strains presentation (colossal). True aesthetic sublimity requires absence of purposive failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical Sublime (unit-expansion leading to the Idea of infinity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of the mathematically Sublime occur when the Imagination is given successively larger units (tree → mountain → earth diameter → planetary system → Milky Way), arriving at the idea of an immeasurable whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The feeling here arises less from large numerical magnitude and more from the Imagination ever arriving at yet greater units—this progression contributes to the Idea of the infinite and to the aesthetic experience of the sublime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of the satisfaction in judgments upon the Sublime (pain + pleasure = respect)
rubrics_metrics.description: The feeling of incapacity to attain an Idea is RESPECT: a painful awareness of the Imagination's inadequacy combined with pleasure from conformity with rational Ideas; the sublime moves the mind (vibration) whereas the beautiful rests it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating sublime experiences, note the mixed affective character—a painful sense of limitation that simultaneously testifies to a higher, purposive rational faculty. Sublimity is experienced as both negative (inadequacy) and positive (respect, pleasure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dynamic Sublime: Nature regarded as Might
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature considered as might that excites fear (but over which we have no dominion) is dynamically sublime: it raises energies and discovers in us a non-sensuous faculty of resistance when we judge it from a position of safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dynamic sublime requires the subject to be in security (we 'call these objects sublime, because they raise the energies of the soul'). Examples: storms, volcanoes, the tumultuous ocean, waterfalls. The aesthetic judgement depends on imagining resistance where actual resistance would be vain, and on the subject's capacity to contemn nature in thought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modal requirement: susceptibility to Ideas and moral feeling (cultural prerequisite)
rubrics_metrics.description: Judging the sublime requires a susceptibility of mind for Ideas (moral feeling); without this cultural/moral development the uneducated perceive only terror, not sublimity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect less universal agreement about the sublime than about beauty; the judgement presumes a moral feeling and a degree of culture. In evaluative contexts, treat claims of sublimity as carrying a conditional universal aspiration (we 'claim' necessity because we presuppose moral feeling in others).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sublime as reference of Imagination to Reason (contrast with the Beautiful)
rubrics_metrics.description: In judging the Beautiful the Imagination is harmonised with the Understanding (concepts); in judging the Sublime the Imagination is referred to Reason (Ideas).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this diagnostic distinction when classifying an aesthetic reaction: does the experience orient imagination toward conceptual harmony (beauty) or toward Ideas and the infinite (sublime)? That relation determines the kind of aesthetic judgement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aesthetic estimation requires comprehension in one intuition (coexistence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aesthetical comprehension aims to receive the manifold in a unity of intuition—making coexistence intuitible—whereas apprehension is temporal progression; forcing comprehension of a large quantum in one intuition is a subjective violence that produces the feeling of the sublime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging magnitude aesthetically, check whether the relevant mental operation is an attempt to grasp many elements simultaneously (coexistence) rather than successively (progress). The tension between time-bound apprehension and atemporal comprehension is central to the sublime.
